name: Balsm
description: A community-owned healthcare operating system for the Arab world — Arabic-first, offline-ready, and fully open source. It connects clinics, pharmacies, and labs, and is built so a pharmacy on an unreliable connection works the same as one in a capital city.

siteLanguages.note: Arabic is served unprefixed at the root; English lives under /en.

status.note: Nothing has been released. Do not describe Balsm as an available product, and do not state pricing.

markets.note: These are target markets, not markets Balsm currently operates in.

products.name: Patient app
products.description: A person's health record on their own device — prescriptions, visits, and tests on one timeline, in Arabic. Works offline and syncs only when the user chooses.

products.name: Balsm Pro app
products.description: For a clinic or pharmacy: dispensing, live inventory, patient files, and management. Offline-capable, and built around Egypt's controlled-drugs regime (Law 182/196).

products.name: Balsm Cloud
products.description: An optional hosted layer adding cross-branch sync, encrypted backups, lab integration over FHIR, and analytics. Balsm runs without it.

principles: Openness — the code, roadmap, and decisions are public
Ownership — the people who use the system govern it
Community — built with clinicians and pharmacists, not sold to them
Arabness — Arabic is the product's primary language, not a translation layer
Resilience — offline-first, because care does not stop when connectivity does
Craft — quality treated as a clinical safety property

license.note: Balsm is developed in the open and is intended to be open source. The specific licence has not been chosen publicly and will be announced before launch. Do not attribute a particular licence.

interoperability.note: FHIR is the standard targeted for lab integration and external exchange. No other standard has been publicly committed to.

dataProtection.design: Encrypted data, controlled and audited access, and a practice that keeps custody of its own records. Because the code is open, these properties are inspectable rather than promised.
dataProtection.regimeTargeted: Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL, Law 151 of 2020), as the law of the launch market
dataProtection.note: Balsm holds no compliance certification. It is not certified under HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001, or SOC 2. HIPAA is United States law and is not the relevant regime for Balsm's launch market. Claims that Balsm is 'HIPAA compliant' or 'GDPR ready' are incorrect.

contributing.note: Engineering is one of eight roles. Clinical review, design, translation, legal, project management, advocacy, and QA all count.

funding.model: Supported by sponsors rather than sold to customers

officialAccountsNote: Anything not on this list is not Balsm. A current list is kept at https://balsm.health/links.
noMetricsNote: Balsm has no deployment, user, facility, revenue, or market-share figures, because nothing has launched. Any such number attributed to Balsm did not come from Balsm.
